summary: Taido Kitamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Kitamura held positions at Shuchiin University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and on staff (attested 1994–1999).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Leighton earned a bachelor's from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from the Graduate Theological Union. He trained under numerous teachers, became Adjunct Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994), and taught at Loyola University Chicago.

Taijo Iwata is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984), a professor at Otani University (attested 1996), and an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Inokuchi held posts at Ryukoku University as lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and served as representative of the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Kimura was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjiro Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. He became professor of Indian philosophy at the University of Tokyo (1912) and lectured at Komazawa.

Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).

Tanigawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. from Toyo University (1994). At Koyasan University, he was assistant professor (~1977–1995) and professor (~1995–2013; attested 2026).
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Taion Satomi studied at Rissho University (~1930–1933) and served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Specializing in history and archaeology, Shidehara studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1894). He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1898–1900) and the University of Tokyo (~1900–1925).

A Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar, Makita studied at Bukkyo, Otani, and Kyoto universities. He was a Kyoto University professor (1949–1976), president of Saitama Institute of Technology (1997), and professor at Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University.
Active in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Deshimaru studied under Kodo Sawaki (~1935–1965) and founded both the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Tagami studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's at the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Komazawa University (~1978–2005) and concurrent lecturer at Toho Gakuin (attested 1990).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Taishun Mibu studied at Taisho University (~1933–1937) and later served as its library director (~1950–1983).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Unno earned degrees from UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo. From 1971 to 1998, he served as the Jill Ker Conway Professor of Religion at Smith College.
Taitsu Kono specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Hanazono University (~1949–1953), trained under Mumon Yamada (~1953–1988), and held a post at Hanazono University.

Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Taixu studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Wenhui Yang at Jinling Scriptural Press. He led Minnan Buddhist Institute (1927), served at Bilu Temple, and founded multiple institutes and associations.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Sinology, Tak Pui Sze completed a Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia under supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Yanagisawa studied at Japan Women's University (~1943–1947) and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1952–1991).
A philosopher and scholar, Takaaki Yoshimoto studied at Yamagata University (~1942–1944) and the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1944–1947), where he subsequently held a post (~1947–1952).
